title: Queen Maria Carolina of Naples and Sicily: three letters partly in cipher, 1809-1812, with a partial decipherment noted (private collection, declared of historical interest 2018)
correspondents: Maria Carolina d'Asburgo Lorena, queen of Naples and Sicily -> unknown (recipient not named; no. 10 also holds the draft reply)
shelfmark: Private owner; Lettere autografe di Maria Carolina d'Asburgo Lorena (14 letters, 1794-1814), Archivi Nazionali ca_9568899, supervised by the Soprintendenza archivistica e bibliografica dell'Emilia-Romagna (Bologna); items 8, 9 and 10
folio_note: Item 8: s.l., 6 Mar 1809, 2 cc., 'la seconda parte e in cifra con parziale decodificazione'. Item 9: Palermo, 1 Jun 1810, 2 cc., 'parte in cifra con parziale decodificazione', on the marriages of her two daughters. Item 10: s.l., 17 Apr and 25 May 1812, 2 cc., partly in cipher with partial decodification, worries about the Kingdom, with the draft reply. Items 1 and 2 (Caserta 13 May 1794, Naples 6 Sep 1794) announce a cipher sheet 'che non risulta allegato' (not present).
status: Description only (Archivi Nazionali fonds record, read 6 Nov 2026). The catalogue notes a partial decodification with each letter, so these are not wholly unread, but how much is read and by whom is not stated. No images online (fonds-level record, no units, no Mirador). Not on DECODE (known.py 'Maria Carolina': no hits).
why: The queen's own cipher during the Sicilian exile (1806-14), written while the Bourbon court at Palermo ran its foreign affairs through her correspondence with Vienna; the partial decodifications give cribs for a full reading of three letters.
score_note: Scored from the Archivi Nazionali description during the 6 Nov 2026 Naples/Palermo sweep (research/sweep_2026-11_naples_palermo/); not viewed
verify: Ask the Soprintendenza archivistica e bibliografica dell'Emilia-Romagna (Bologna) for the owner and for photographs of items 8-10; check whether the editors of Maria Carolina's letters (Io, la Regina, 2020) print these.
prior_art: open as far as checked (6 Nov 2026: web search for the fonds and the cipher passages found nothing; cryptiana has no Maria Carolina page found; printed edition not searched in full)
access_note: private owner under the Emilia-Romagna Soprintendenza; no images online; access needs a request to the Soprintendenza

date: first two decades of the 19th century (the Misc. Arch. list gives 1861, probably the date of the extract or deposit)
title: ASPa Miscellanea archivistica II serie n. 262: 'Lettera in codice e in cifrato' of the early 19th century
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Palermo, Miscellanea archivistica, II serie, n. 262 (inventory n. 152, unita 716, ed. S. Falletta)
folio_note: One entry in the printed list: 'Lettera in codice e in cifrato risalente al primo ventennio del XIX secolo'. The next entry (n. 263) is a different item: an 18th-century cipher with its alphabet and a typed transcription by Dr Marco Modica, extracted from Ministero luogotenenziale, Polizia, b. 1679 (read; not a row).
status: Description only: the inventory (read through the Wayback copy of the Palermo SAASSIPA PDF) does not say whether a decipherment is attached; the neighbouring n. 263 carries a transcription, n. 262 does not. Not on DECODE (known.py: no hit). Palermo's own hosts were not reachable from this machine, so whether the Palermo digital library holds scans of this unit was not checked.
why: A Sicilian code-and-cipher letter of the Bourbon years (revolution of 1820 or the exile period); no key is listed.
